title: Localization cocone maps are determined by their zeroth legs
statement: In any preadditive category, let c and d be cocones on the scalar sequence of an object K. Suppose multiplication by ℓ on d.pt is invertible. If g:c.pt→d.pt commutes with the zeroth leg, it commutes with every leg. Definitions and notation: [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope].

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), referring to Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2; scalar localization telescope

proof.text: Induct on n. Each cocone identifies its nth leg with ℓ times the next leg. Scalar multiplication is central, so the induction hypothesis implies the next-leg equality after composition with multiplication by ℓ on d.pt. Cancel this isomorphism.

proof_origin.note: B2: explicit scalar telescope construction and categorical compatibility. This auxiliary declaration is proved in the delivery, not a new assumption.
